title: setDepletionDuration(1) is a one-tx rug surface: owner can collapse the depletion window so the next _updatePool drains rewardBalance to a single coordinated staker
rootCause: `setDepletionDuration` accepts any `_duration > 0`. With `_duration = 1`, `rewardPerSecond = rewardBalance * PRECISION`. The very next `_updatePool` (any subsequent interaction) credits the entire `rewardBalance` to `accStablePerShare` in a single block. There is no two-step gate on this setter (unlike `setDesiredAPY`), no minimum-duration floor, and no timelock — strictly more dangerous than the APY setter yet with weaker access controls.
impactSummary: Owner (or compromised owner key) can drain the entire stable reward pool to whichever stakers exist at the moment of the next `_updatePool`. Bundleable with a flash-stake to capture the full `rewardBalance` in one MEV bundle — a one-block rug of every reward funder's contribution.
preservedDetails: ECON-002 carries the strongest framing: explicit one-tx flash-drain scenario with profit math, asymmetry vs setDesiredAPY's two-step gate. PATTERN-006 contributes the CENTRALIZATION-ADMIN structural match and 'owner-economic-acceleration' framing.
remediation: Add `require(_duration >= MIN_DEPLETION_DURATION)`; add a two-step gate symmetric with setDesiredAPY; wrap in timelock so honest stakers can pauseWithdraw before a malicious change.
consolidationRationale: Both target the same setter on the same line. PATTERN-006 is the structural CENTRALIZATION-ADMIN match; ECON-002 adds the explicit one-tx rug scenario, profit math, and asymmetry vs setDesiredAPY observation.
dedupNotes: Strictly worse than DEDUP-006 (APY-side) because it has no gate at all. Sanitizer / classifier should treat as plausible-High.
